 PVL: Creamline sweeps Farm Fresh, clinches twice-to-beat incentive in semis
 Kennedy Caacbay ,
 ABS-CBN News
 Published November 21, 2026 02:51 PM PHT 
  | 
 Updated November 21, 2026 03:31 PM PHT 
 The Creamline Cool Smashers. PVL Images  MANILA  (UPDATED) — Creamline secured the last twice-to-beat advantage in the semifinals of the 2026-27 Premier Volleyball League (PVL) All-Filipino Conference Siklab series.
 This, as the Cool Smashers swept fellow semis-bound Farm Fresh, 25-19, 25-18, 25-18, during the final game date of the preliminary round on Saturday at the PhilSports Arena in Pasig City.
 The 11-time PVL champions also arrested a three-game slide, regaining their winning form ahead of the Final Four, ending the preliminaries with a 5-3 card and 16 points.
 READ: PVL: Choco Mucho seals Final Four berth by beating PLDT
 “Siyempre, masaya kami lalo na ako at talagang nagtrabaho 'yung team namin. ‘Yung responsibility nila sa loob ng court, ginawa nila,” said head coach Sherwin Meneses during the postgame press conference, praising his players for excellently doing their jobs on the taraflex.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Nearing victory, Jema Galanza fired back-to-back service aces late in Set 3 to install a 23-17 Creamline lead.
 A through-the-block hit from Bernadeth Pons put Creamline on match point, 24-18, while a Bea de Leon closed out the game with a kill block, ending the match in just one hour and 35 minutes.
 “So kami as mga coaches, masaya kami pag ganun naman 'yung tinatrabaho ng mga players. So thankful din kami kasi nakuha namin yung twice-to-beat,” added Meneses.
 READ: PVL: Erika Santos, Vanie Gandler power Capital1 past Galeries to end Siklab series on winning note
 Tots Carlos led the charge with 12 points dealt mostly on attacks, while Pons was the other double-digit scorer for Creamline with 10 points, and Galanza chipped in nine markers.
 They will face their sister team, Choco Mucho, next round for a slot in the finals.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 “Pero siyempre, malayo pa. Mga games, medyo pahigpit nang pahigpit. Pero ready naman ‘yung Creamline. Lagi namang ready ‘yung Creamline,” vowed Meneses.
 Pacing the other side was Trisha Tubu who had 18 points, as the Foxies came so close to achieving the second seed.
 They will finish with a 5-3 card alongside 14 points, settling for a twice-to-win disadvantage against top seed and currently unbeaten Nxled.
